newsitem.title: FRANCE: Traxon optmistic after positive 96 financial resulTS.
newsitem.headline: Traxon optmistic after positive 96 financial resulTS.

text.p: Traxon Europe, the European arm of airfreight information system, Traxon, is optimistic it will remain profitable in 1997 following its first-ever year of profits last year since its creation in 1991.
"We have been in profit month-on-month since July 1996 and the outlook for 1997 as a whole looks promising," Traxon Europe sales and marketing manager, Christian Gillard, told Reuters.

Frankfurt-based Traxon Europe would not be communicating a precise figure on 1996 profits but did confirm a 21 percent increase in turnover on 1995 levels to 6.3 million marks ($3.6 million), he added.
"Growth in turnover is largely due to a reduction in operating costs, an expanding client base and a strong increase in the number of messages transmitted via the system."
Traxon Europe subscriber rates had been cut by ten percent in July 1996 and this scale of decrease would continue annually over the next four years, Gillard added.
"Last year, around eight million electronic messages were transmitted via Traxon Europe and this year our objective is to generate ten million messages," Gillard had said earlier statement.

The full list of Traxon's airline participants worldwide are: Air Canada, Air France, British Airways, Cargolux, Cathay Pacific, Emirates, Finnair, Japan Airlines, KLM, Korean Airlines, Lufthansa, Martinair, Royal Air Maroc, SAS, Singapore Airlines and Swissair.
In addition, Northwest Airlines and Federal Express are linked to Traxon Asia with United Airlines set to follow shortly.
Two other airlines, Austrian Airlines and Air Malta are on the point of joining Traxon while Air India is also showing an interest, Gillard added.
1,879 agents worldwide are linked to Traxon, covering a network of 4,836 offices.
Traxon is organised into two sister companies, Traxon Europe and Traxon Asia
